messages.content: What is the earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?

function.name: get_earliest_reference
function.description: Retrieve the earliest historical reference of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source.description: Source to fetch the reference. Default is 'scriptures'

message.content:
**Earliest non‑Christian historical reference to Jesus Christ** | Source | Date (approx.) | Passage & Context | |--------|----------------|-------------------| | **Flavius Josephus – *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 18, Chapter 3** | 93–94 CE | In the “Testimonium Flavianum” Josephus briefly describes Jesus as a “wise man” who was crucified by Pontius Pilate. The passage reads (in a commonly accepted reconstruction):
“Now there was about this time Jesus, a wise man, if it be lawful to call him a man; for he was a doer of wonderful works, a teacher of people who received the truth with pleasure. He attracted a great number of followers, both Jews and Gentiles. He was crucified by Pilate, but his followers continued to believe in him.”
Scholars generally agree that the core of the passage is authentic, though later Christian interpolations may have added or altered wording. | | **Tacitus – *Annals*, Book 15, Chapter 44** | 116 CE | In a broader discussion of Nero’s persecution of Christians, Tacitus writes: “Christ, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius.” This is the earliest Roman mention of Jesus’ execution. | | **Pliny the Younger – *Letters* (Letter 10.96)** | 112 CE | Pliny, a provincial governor in Bithynia, reports that Christians worshiped Christ as a god. | **Why Josephus is considered the earliest** - The *Testimonium Flavianum* is dated to the 90s CE, roughly 20–30 years after Jesus’ death. - It is the earliest surviving text that mentions Jesus by name and gives a brief account of his life and crucifixion. - While the passage has been subject to scholarly debate regarding later Christian additions, most historians accept that the core reference to Jesus is genuine. **Other early Christian references** - The canonical Gospels (*Matthew*, *Mark*, *Luke*, *John*) were written between ~70 CE and 90 CE. These are the earliest Christian accounts but are theological documents rather than independent historical records. --- ### Bottom line The earliest **historical record** (outside Christian scripture) that mentions Jesus Christ is **Josephus’ *Antiquities of the Jews* (Book 18, Chapter 3)**, written around **93–94 CE**. Subsequent references by Tacitus and Pliny provide corroboration but come slightly later.
